question: Which statement best describes The four transition properties?
options: Transitions only work on properties that have a defined, interpolatable intermediate value — colors, lengths, opacity, transforms, etc. Properties like display, and auto values (e.g. height: auto), are not animatable in the traditional model, which is why people animate max-height or use transforms instead. transitioning all animates every animatable property that changes.

A transition is configured by four longhand properties: transition-property (which CSS property to animate, or all), transition-duration (how long, required for anything to be visible), transition-timing-function (the acceleration curve), and transition-delay (how long to wait before starting). Duration is the only one with no useful default — without it the change is instant.

transition combines all four longhands in one declaration: transition: <property> <duration> <timing-function> <delay>. The first time value parsed is duration, the second is delay. You can list multiple comma-separated transitions to give different properties different timings.

The timing function shapes the rate of change across the duration. linear is constant speed; ease (default) starts slow, speeds up, then slows; ease-in accelerates, ease-out decelerates, ease-in-out does both. cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) defines a fully custom curve, and steps(n) jumps in discrete frames.

question: Which statement best describes The transition shorthand?
options: transition combines all four longhands in one declaration: transition: <property> <duration> <timing-function> <delay>. The first time value parsed is duration, the second is delay. You can list multiple comma-separated transitions to give different properties different timings.

A transition runs whenever the property's computed value changes. The canonical trigger is :hover, but any state change works — :focus, :active, or a JS-toggled class. Put the transition on the BASE selector (not only on :hover) so the change animates both into and out of the state.

transform and opacity are the cheapest properties to animate because the browser can handle them on the compositor (often the GPU) without recalculating layout or repainting. Animating layout properties like width, height, top, or margin triggers reflow on every frame and can cause jank. Prefer translate/scale over top/left/width.

A transition animates a one-shot change between two states and needs a trigger (a value change). A @keyframes animation can run on its own, loop, define many intermediate steps, and play without a state change. Reach for transitions for hover/focus/toggle effects; reach for animations for looping or multi-step motion.
